answer.rationale: The two observed deficits are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which map directly onto the onboarding/activation evidence (memory_31, memory_86, memory_91) rather than onto price. Competitor entry pricing makes promotional_pricing feel urgent, but memory_73 is the memory I trust least on its face: it reports unusually precise paired gains (31% activations, 18% revenue) with no stated effect on retention, churn, or margin, and 'the pricing page was not otherwise altered' reads like a note that other things may have varied. A 40% discount also carries the largest downstream value risk here — anchoring price expectations, degrading revenue quality per account, and attracting exactly the price-sensitive segment the competitor is courting, which is misaligned with 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue.' So I spend one verification pull on memory_73 specifically to see whether that record supports a durable revenue claim or only a short-window activation bump. I spend the second on memory_86, because it is the memory I intend to act on and it was consolidated at day 52 under pre-competitor conditions; I want the original record to confirm the lift was in completion and time-to-value rather than a vanity completion metric, and to see the segment and duration. memory_57 and memory_44 are plausible but address neither observed deficit — referral incentives target established customers and sales-assist targets enterprise, while the bleeding is self-serve SMB. Uncertainty I am carrying and not resolving: all of this memory predates the competitor launch, so prior effect sizes may not transfer; a 4-6% QoQ decline could partly be mix shift from losing price-sensitive accounts rather than a broken funnel. I therefore intend a standard experiment with proper holdout and a revenue-quality readout, not a broad rollout, and I will revise toward activation_messaging if verification shows memory_86's lift was narrower than stated. If memory_73's source record turns out to be clean, well-powered, and to include retention and margin data, I would reconsider a small_guarded_test on pricing — but I would not lead with it on the current record.
